title: Mary, looking back
hookLine: a girl who said yes and kept it all in her heart
tomorrow: five objects hold one whole week. which five?

cards: Some news goes straight into a screenshot that never gets sent. Too big to explain, too early to understand. Luke's answer to what you do with news like that is a young woman in Nazareth.
An angel greets her with news nobody could explain, and she answers: “Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.” Yes, first. Understanding later, and slowly.

teach.b: After the birth, shepherds turn up with a story about angels, and everyone wonders. Then Luke adds: “But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.” Kept and pondered.
Not solved. Held. When Jesus is twelve, he stays behind in Jerusalem, and his parents search until they find him in the temple.

teach.h: THEY UNDERSTOOD NOT, AND SHE KEPT IT.
teach.b: He answers them, and Luke admits, “they understood not the saying which he spake unto them.” Then: “but his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.”
Here's the detail to tell a friend: Luke says it twice, once after wonderful news and once after words she didn't understand. She kept both. The Gospels keep finding her.
At a wedding in Cana, when the wine runs out, she tells the servants, “Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.”
At the worst hour, “there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother.” And in Acts she's praying with the disciples after he's gone. Christians honor her in different ways.
Catholic and Orthodox Christians ask her prayers and keep her feasts; Protestant churches honor her as an example of trust and pray to God directly.
Luke's lines are the same in all their Bibles: a yes, and a long keeping.

how: Catholic and Orthodox Christians honor Mary with prayers such as the Hail Mary and with feast days; Protestant churches honor her as a model of faith, especially at Christmas, and pray to God directly.

o: Jesus's sister, who led the church after him
the mother of Jesus, who said yes and kept it all
a prophet who wrote one of the four Gospels

p: and pondered them in her heart

s: Luke tells us exactly how old Mary was
Luke never gives her age. he calls her a virgin espoused to a man named Joseph.
Luke says twice that Mary kept these things in her heart
once after the shepherds, once after the temple, when she understood not.
Mary is at the cross in John's Gospel
now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother.

games.q: a test result comes back: "we'll know more in a month." your friend wants to guess the worst together tonight. what fits Mary's way in Luke?
o: research every possibility tonight until you feel certain.
keep it and ponder it; it doesn't have to be solved tonight.
put it completely out of mind until the month is over.
games.why: Mary kept what she didn't understand and pondered it. not solving it, not forgetting it: holding it.

practice: Find one small thing you can close your hand around: a ring, a key, a smooth stone. Hold it and feel its weight, its edges, the way it slowly warms.

Let it stand for one yes you've given, to a person, a promise, a faith, whose ending you don't know yet. Keep your hand closed around it, the way Luke says Mary kept things: not working it out, just holding it.
If you pray, you can say her words, be it unto me according to thy word, and rest there.

wordCard.voice: Mary. The mother of Jesus, who said yes first and kept in her heart what she didn't yet understand.

orig.note: the Greek for 'kept' in Luke 2:19: Mary kept all these things.

carryVoice: Carry this: keep it in your heart, because some things are for holding before they're for solving. Day seventeen fifty-four, done.
